title: Cumulative duty
source_text:
### ORO.FTL.210(a), (c) — regulatory requirements

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(a)   The total duty periods to which a crew member may be assigned shall not exceed:
      (1)   60 duty hours in any 7 consecutive days;
      (2)   110 duty hours in any 14 consecutive days; and
      (3)   190 duty hours in any 28 consecutive days, spread as evenly as practicable throughout
            that period.

(c)   Post-flight duty shall count as duty period. The operator shall specify in its operations manual
      the minimum time period for post-flight duties.
```

### ORO.FTL.105 definitions (10, 11)

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(10) ‘duty’ means any task that a crew member performs for the operator, including flight duty,
     administrative work, giving or receiving training and checking, positioning, and some elements
     of standby;

(11) ‘duty period’ means a period which starts when a crew member is required by an operator to
     report for or to commence a duty and ends when that person is free of all duties, including post-flight duty;
```

### ORO.FTL.225(c) — airport standby accounting

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(c)   airport standby shall count in full as duty period for the purpose of points ORO.FTL.210 and
      ORO.FTL.235;
```

### CS FTL.1.225(b)(3) — other standby accounting

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(3)   25 % of time spent on standby other than airport standby counts as duty time for the
            purpose of ORO.FTL.210;
```

### AMC1 ORO.FTL.210(c) — acceptable means of compliance

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
AMC1 ORO.FTL.210(c) Flight times and duty periods

POST-FLIGHT DUTIES
The operator should specify post-flight duty times taking into account the type of operation, the size
and type of aircraft and the airport conditions.
```

### CS FTL.1.230(b) — reserve accounting

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(b)   Reserve times do not count as duty period for the purpose of ORO.FTL.210 and ORO.FTL.235.
```
notes: Edition/scope note (explanatory, not a quotation): EASA Easy Access Rules for Air Operations, Revision 24, March 2026, preserved official edition; PDF viewer and printed page numbers agree. ORO.FTL.100 (p. 854) addresses CAT aeroplanes. CS FTL.1.100 (p. 874) covers scheduled and charter aeroplane CAT, excluding EMS, air taxi and single-pilot operations. ORO.FTL.125 (p. 865) requires an operation-appropriate, competent-authority-approved flight time specification scheme; preserve applicable approved-scheme choices and operator procedures. ORO requirements, CS certification specifications, AMC acceptable means of compliance and GM guidance have different status. This source record makes no claim about amendments after Revision 24.

Consecutive-day boundary/time-zone and cross-midnight attribution semantics must be explicit; do not silently replace them with roster weeks or rolling-hour windows. Avoid double-counting overlapping activities. “Spread as evenly as practicable” is an additional qualitative obligation, not another numerical cap.
illustrative_scenarios: For the same crew member, 60:00 duty in any seven consecutive days meets the ceiling and 60:01 exceeds it; likewise test equality and one minute over 110:00/14 days and 190:00/28 days.
A seven-day window crossing a roster-week boundary is still checked, using the documented consecutive-day and cross-midnight attribution convention.
Eight hours of airport standby adds 8:00 to cumulative duty; eight hours of other standby adds 2:00; reserve adds zero under the selected CS.
Post-flight work contributes to full duty, without adding operating activity durations a second time; record a separate assessment of “spread as evenly as practicable”.
scenario_note: These scenarios illustrate source meaning and interpretation choices for documentary review. They are not acceptance requirements for a local evaluator or executable compliance tests.

title: Cumulative operating flight time
source_text:
### ORO.FTL.210(b) — regulatory requirement

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(b)   The total flight time of the sectors on which an individual crew member is assigned as an
      operating crew member shall not exceed:
      (1)   100 hours of flight time in any 28 consecutive days;
      (2)   900 hours of flight time in any calendar year; and
      (3)   1 000 hours of flight time in any 12 consecutive calendar months.
```

### ORO.FTL.105 definitions (13, 17)

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(13) ‘flight time’ means, for aeroplanes, the time between an aircraft first moving from its parking
     place for the purpose of taking off until it comes to rest on the designated parking position and
     all engines or propellers are shut down.

(17) ‘operating crew member’ means a crew member carrying out duties in an aircraft during a
     sector;
```

### GM1 ORO.FTL.105(17) — explanatory guidance

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
GM1 ORO.FTL.105(17) Definitions

OPERATING CREW MEMBER
A person on board an aircraft is either a crew member or a passenger. If a crew member is not a
passenger on board an aircraft he/she should be considered as ‘carrying out duties’. The crew member
remains an operating crew member during in-flight rest. In-flight rest counts in full as FDP, and for the
purpose of ORO.FTL.210.
```
notes: Edition/scope note (explanatory, not a quotation): EASA Easy Access Rules for Air Operations, Revision 24, March 2026, preserved official edition; PDF viewer and printed page numbers agree. ORO.FTL.100 (p. 854) addresses CAT aeroplanes. CS FTL.1.100 (p. 874) covers scheduled and charter aeroplane CAT, excluding EMS, air taxi and single-pilot operations. ORO.FTL.125 (p. 865) requires an operation-appropriate, competent-authority-approved flight time specification scheme; preserve applicable approved-scheme choices and operator procedures. ORO requirements, CS certification specifications, AMC acceptable means of compliance and GM guidance have different status. This source record makes no claim about amendments after Revision 24.

Count the individual crew member’s operating sectors, including in-flight rest; positioning passenger time does not become operating time. Calendar year and twelve consecutive calendar months need distinct calendar semantics; neither is a fixed 365-day duration.
illustrative_scenarios: A crew member positioning as a passenger on a three-hour flight adds zero to that person’s operating-flight total; an operating crew member’s in-flight rest remains included.
100:00 in 28 consecutive days, 900:00 in a calendar year and 1 000:00 in twelve consecutive calendar months meet their respective ceilings; one additional minute exceeds each.
A December–January roster starts a new calendar-year total while preserving applicable twelve-consecutive-calendar-month checks.
A twelve-calendar-month window including leap-year February follows actual month boundaries, rather than a fixed 365-day duration.
scenario_note: These scenarios illustrate source meaning and interpretation choices for documentary review. They are not acceptance requirements for a local evaluator or executable compliance tests.

### ORO.FTL.105 definitions (1, 2, 12, 24)

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(1)    ‘acclimatised’ means a state in which a crew member’s circadian biological clock is synchronised
       to the time zone where the crew member is. A crew member is considered to be acclimatised
       to a 2-hour wide time zone surrounding the local time at the point of departure. When the local
       time at the place where a duty commences differs by more than 2 hours from the local time at
       the place where the next duty starts, the crew member, for the calculation of the maximum
       daily flight duty period, is considered to be acclimatised in accordance with the values in the
       Table 1.
       Table 1

        Time difference (h) between reference
          time and local time where the crew           Time elapsed since reporting at reference time
             member starts the next duty
                                                 <48          48–71:59     72–95:59    96–119:59       ≥120
        <4                                       B            D            D           D               D
        ≤6                                       B            X            D           D               D
        ≤9                                       B            X            X           D               D
        ≤12                                      B            X            X           X               D

       ‘B’ means acclimatised to the local time of the departure time zone,
       ‘D’ means acclimatised to the local time where the crew member starts his/her next duty, and
       ‘X’ means that a crew member is in an unknown state of acclimatisation.

(2)    ‘reference time’ means the local time at the reporting point situated in a 2-hour wide time zone
       band around the local time where a crew member is acclimatised;

(12) ‘flight duty period ('FDP')’ means a period that commences when a crew member is required to
     report for duty, which includes a sector or a series of sectors, and finishes when the aircraft
     finally comes to rest and the engines are shut down, at the end of the last sector on which the
     crew member acts as an operating crew member;

(24) ‘sector’ means the segment of an FDP between an aircraft first moving for the purpose of taking
     off until it comes to rest after landing on the designated parking position.
```

### GM1–3 ORO.FTL.105(1) and GM1 ORO.FTL.105(2) — explanatory guidance

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
GM1 ORO.FTL.105(1) Definitions

ACCLIMATISED
(a)   A crew member remains acclimatised to the local time of his or her reference time during
      47 hours 59 minutes after reporting no matter how many time zones he/she has crossed.

(b)   The maximum daily FDP for acclimatised crew members is determined by using table 1 of
      ORO.FTL.205(b)(1) with the reference time of the point of departure. As soon as 48 hours have
      elapsed, the state of acclimatisation is derived from the time elapsed since reporting at
      reference time and the number of time zones crossed.
(c)   A crew member is considered to be in an unknown state of acclimatisation after the first 48
      hours of the rotation have elapsed unless he or she remains in the first arrival destination time
      zone (either for rest or any duties) in accordance with the table in ORO.FTL.105(1).
(d)   Should a crew member’s rotation include additional duties that end in a different time zone
      than his or her first arrival destination’s time zone while he or she is considered to be in an
      unknown state of acclimatisation, then the crew member remains in an unknown state of
      acclimatisation until he or she:
      (1)    has taken the rest period required by CS FTL.1.235(b)(3) at home base;
      (2)    has taken the rest period required by CS FTL.1.235(b)(3) at the new location; or
      (3)    has been undertaking duties starting at and returning to the time zone of the new
             location until he or she becomes acclimatised in accordance with the values in the table
             in ORO.FTL.105(1).
             To determine the state of acclimatisation, the two following criteria should be applied:
             (i)    the greater of the time differences between the time zone where he or she was
                    last acclimatised or the local time of his or her last departure point and the new
                    location; and
             (ii)   the time elapsed since reporting at home base for the first time during the rotation.

GM2 ORO.FTL.105(1) Definitions

ACCLIMATISED ‘POINT OF DEPARTURE’
The point of departure refers to the reporting point for a flight duty period or positioning duty after a
rest period.

GM3 ORO.FTL.105(1) Definitions

ACCLIMATISED ‘TIME ELAPSED SINCE REPORTING AT REFERENCE TIME’
The time elapsed since reporting at reference time for operations applying CS FTL.1.235(b)(3)(ii) at
home base refers to the time elapsed since reporting for the first time at home base for a rotation.

GM1 ORO.FTL.105(2) Definitions

REFERENCE TIME
(a)   Reference time refers to reporting points in a 2-hour wide time zone band around the local time
      where a crew member is acclimatised.
(b)   Example: A crew member is acclimatised to the local time in Helsinki and reports for duty in
      London. The reference time is the local time in London.
```
notes: Edition/scope note (explanatory, not a quotation): EASA Easy Access Rules for Air Operations, Revision 24, March 2026, preserved official edition; PDF viewer and printed page numbers agree. ORO.FTL.100 (p. 854) addresses CAT aeroplanes. CS FTL.1.100 (p. 874) covers scheduled and charter aeroplane CAT, excluding EMS, air taxi and single-pilot operations. ORO.FTL.125 (p. 865) requires an operation-appropriate, competent-authority-approved flight time specification scheme; preserve applicable approved-scheme choices and operator procedures. ORO requirements, CS certification specifications, AMC acceptable means of compliance and GM guidance have different status. This source record makes no claim about amendments after Revision 24.

Table 1 is included with the exact printed row labels (<4, ≤6, ≤9, ≤12) and B/D/X meanings; determine its applicable ordered band rather than treating overlapping printed upper bounds as independent predicates. Table 4 needs the stated continuously monitored FRM safety performance. Keep reference-time and acclimatisation history per person.

Editorial cross-reference preserved verbatim: GM1 ORO.FTL.105(1)(b) says “table 1 of ORO.FTL.205(b)(1)” although the displayed acclimatised FDP table in this edition is labelled Table 2. Do not silently change the quoted source.

This source family selects the basic maximum; cabin reporting differences, night-duty controls, extensions, discretion and delayed reporting remain separate applicable dependencies. Specify treatment of seconds and out-of-table inputs explicitly.
illustrative_scenarios: For one or two operating sectors and acclimatised crew, reference-time start 13:29 permits 13:00 FDP; start 13:30 permits 12:45, so 13:00 then exceeds the cap.
Table 2 sector grouping is exact: one and two sectors use the same cap, the third sector reduces it by 00:30, and every printed cell respects the 09:00 floor; compare all Table 2–4 cells.

Unknown-state crew with one or two sectors receive 11:00 under Table 3 and 12:00 only with the required continuously monitored FRM safety-performance condition; both unknown-state tables end at eight sectors.
Acclimatisation at 47:59 and 48:00 follows reference-time/rotation history and the Table 1 B/D/X transition; additional time-zone changes must not reset history arbitrarily.

Pre-operating positioning before two operating flights does not produce a third operating sector. Unsupported table domains and missing required facts yield an explicit invalid/unevaluable result, not silent compliance.

title: Positioning accounting
source_text:
### ORO.FTL.215 — regulatory requirement

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
ORO.FTL.215 Positioning

If an operator positions a crew member, the following shall apply:
(a)   positioning after reporting but prior to operating shall be counted as FDP but shall not count as
      a sector;
(b)   all time spent on positioning shall count as duty period.
```

### ORO.FTL.105 definitions (18, 12, 17, 24)

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(18) ‘positioning’ means the transferring of a non-operating crew member from one place to
     another, at the behest of the operator, excluding:
      —      the time of travel from a private place of rest to the designated reporting place at home
             base and vice versa, and
      —      the time for local transfer from a place of rest to the commencement of duty and vice
             versa;

(12) ‘flight duty period ('FDP')’ means a period that commences when a crew member is required to
     report for duty, which includes a sector or a series of sectors, and finishes when the aircraft
     finally comes to rest and the engines are shut down, at the end of the last sector on which the
     crew member acts as an operating crew member;

(17) ‘operating crew member’ means a crew member carrying out duties in an aircraft during a
     sector;

(24) ‘sector’ means the segment of an FDP between an aircraft first moving for the purpose of taking
     off until it comes to rest after landing on the designated parking position.
```
notes: Edition/scope note (explanatory, not a quotation): EASA Easy Access Rules for Air Operations, Revision 24, March 2026, preserved official edition; PDF viewer and printed page numbers agree. ORO.FTL.100 (p. 854) addresses CAT aeroplanes. CS FTL.1.100 (p. 874) covers scheduled and charter aeroplane CAT, excluding EMS, air taxi and single-pilot operations. ORO.FTL.125 (p. 865) requires an operation-appropriate, competent-authority-approved flight time specification scheme; preserve applicable approved-scheme choices and operator procedures. ORO requirements, CS certification specifications, AMC acceptable means of compliance and GM guidance have different status. This source record makes no claim about amendments after Revision 24.

The positioning definition excludes ordinary travel between private rest and the home-base reporting place and local transfers between rest and duty. Distinguish transport purpose and person-specific operating role. Positioning after the last operating sector extends full duty, not that person’s FDP.
illustrative_scenarios: Report 06:00, position 06:30–08:00, operate 09:00–11:00, release 11:30: FDP is 5:00, full duty is 5:30, and the operating-sector count is one.
Additional positioning after the last operating sector extends full duty while the FDP endpoint remains the last operating-sector parking/shutdown endpoint.
A private-home/rest-to-home-base reporting commute and a local hotel transfer are excluded from positioning; classify the journey by purpose, not solely by its transport category.
scenario_note: These scenarios illustrate source meaning and interpretation choices for documentary review. They are not acceptance requirements for a local evaluator or executable compliance tests.

title: Minimum rest at home base
source_text:
### ORO.FTL.235(a), (b) — regulatory requirement and derogation dependency

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(a)   Minimum rest period at home base.
      (1)    The minimum rest period provided before undertaking an FDP starting at home base shall
             be at least as long as the preceding duty period, or 12 hours, whichever is greater.
      (2)    By way of derogation from point (1), the minimum rest provided under point (b) applies
             if the operator provides suitable accommodation to the crew member at home base.
(b)   Minimum rest period away from home base.
      The minimum rest period provided before undertaking an FDP starting away from home base
      shall be at least as long as the preceding duty period, or 10 hours, whichever is greater. This
      period shall include an 8-hour sleep opportunity in addition to the time for travelling and
      physiological needs.
```

### ORO.FTL.105 definitions (21, 14, 4, 11)

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(21) ‘rest period’ means a continuous, uninterrupted and defined period of time, following duty or
     prior to duty, during which a crew member is free of all duties, standby and reserve.

(14) ‘home base’ means the location, assigned by the operator to the crew member, from where the
     crew member normally starts and ends a duty period or a series of duty periods and where,

      under normal circumstances, the operator is not responsible for the accommodation of the
      crew member concerned;

(4)   ‘suitable accommodation’ means, for the purpose of standby, split duty and rest, a separate
      room for each crew member located in a quiet environment and equipped with a bed, which is
      sufficiently ventilated, has a device for regulating temperature and light intensity, and access to
      food and drink;

(11) ‘duty period’ means a period which starts when a crew member is required by an operator to
     report for or to commence a duty and ends when that person is free of all duties, including post-flight duty;
```

### GM1 ORO.FTL.235(a)(2) — explanatory guidance

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
GM1 ORO.FTL.235(a)(2) Rest periods

MINIMUM REST PERIOD AT HOME BASE IF SUITABLE ACCOMMODATION IS PROVIDED
An operator may apply the minimum rest period away from home base during a rotation which
includes a rest period at a crew member’s home base. This applies only if the crew member does not
rest at his/her residence, or temporary accommodation, because the operator provides suitable
accommodation. This type of roster is known as "back-to-back operation".
```
notes: Edition/scope note (explanatory, not a quotation): EASA Easy Access Rules for Air Operations, Revision 24, March 2026, preserved official edition; PDF viewer and printed page numbers agree. ORO.FTL.100 (p. 854) addresses CAT aeroplanes. CS FTL.1.100 (p. 874) covers scheduled and charter aeroplane CAT, excluding EMS, air taxi and single-pilot operations. ORO.FTL.125 (p. 865) requires an operation-appropriate, competent-authority-approved flight time specification scheme; preserve applicable approved-scheme choices and operator procedures. ORO requirements, CS certification specifications, AMC acceptable means of compliance and GM guidance have different status. This source record makes no claim about amendments after Revision 24.

The succeeding FDP must start at home base; link the preceding complete duty and uninterrupted rest for the same person. The suitable-accommodation derogation routes to the away-base requirement, including protected sleep, travel and physiological needs. Reduced rest and compensatory provisions require separate eligibility and effects.
illustrative_scenarios: Before a home-base FDP after 13:00 full duty, 12:59 rest fails and 13:00 meets the ordinary duration minimum; after 10:00 duty, the ordinary minimum is 12:00.

An operator-provided suitable-accommodation derogation at home base applies the away-base requirement, including the protected sleep opportunity; a generic accommodation flag alone does not establish that derogation.
A nominally sufficient rest interrupted by duty, standby or reserve fails the uninterrupted rest definition; the prior duty must include post-flight work.
scenario_note: These scenarios illustrate source meaning and interpretation choices for documentary review. They are not acceptance requirements for a local evaluator or executable compliance tests.

title: Minimum rest away from home base
source_text:
### ORO.FTL.235(b) — regulatory requirement

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(b)   Minimum rest period away from home base.
      The minimum rest period provided before undertaking an FDP starting away from home base
      shall be at least as long as the preceding duty period, or 10 hours, whichever is greater. This
      period shall include an 8-hour sleep opportunity in addition to the time for travelling and
      physiological needs.
```

### ORO.FTL.105 definitions (21, 11, 4)

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(21) ‘rest period’ means a continuous, uninterrupted and defined period of time, following duty or
     prior to duty, during which a crew member is free of all duties, standby and reserve.

(11) ‘duty period’ means a period which starts when a crew member is required by an operator to
     report for or to commence a duty and ends when that person is free of all duties, including post-flight duty;

(4)   ‘suitable accommodation’ means, for the purpose of standby, split duty and rest, a separate
      room for each crew member located in a quiet environment and equipped with a bed, which is
      sufficiently ventilated, has a device for regulating temperature and light intensity, and access to
      food and drink;
```

### AMC1 ORO.FTL.235(b) — acceptable means of compliance

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
AMC1 ORO.FTL.235(b) Rest periods

MINIMUM REST PERIOD AWAY FROM HOME BASE
The time allowed for physiological needs should be 1 hour. Consequently, if the travelling time to the
suitable accommodation is more than 30 minutes, the operator should increase the rest period by
twice the amount of difference of travelling time above 30 minutes.
```
notes: Edition/scope note (explanatory, not a quotation): EASA Easy Access Rules for Air Operations, Revision 24, March 2026, preserved official edition; PDF viewer and printed page numbers agree. ORO.FTL.100 (p. 854) addresses CAT aeroplanes. CS FTL.1.100 (p. 874) covers scheduled and charter aeroplane CAT, excluding EMS, air taxi and single-pilot operations. ORO.FTL.125 (p. 865) requires an operation-appropriate, competent-authority-approved flight time specification scheme; preserve applicable approved-scheme choices and operator procedures. ORO requirements, CS certification specifications, AMC acceptable means of compliance and GM guidance have different status. This source record makes no claim about amendments after Revision 24.

Retain the independent protected 8-hour sleep opportunity as well as the duration requirement. AMC says one hour for physiological needs and twice the travel excess above 30 minutes. The quoted wording does not explicitly resolve calculation order when preceding duty already exceeds 10 hours: record the approved interpretation instead of silently choosing max(previous duty, 10 h + adjustment) versus max(previous duty, 10 h) + adjustment. A 45-minute transfer with short preceding duty produces a 10:30 floor; a 12-hour preceding duty distinguishes those calculation orders.
illustrative_scenarios: After short preceding duty with a 45-minute transfer to suitable accommodation, a nominal 10:00 rest fails and 10:30 meets the travel-adjusted floor under the stated symmetric-travel assumption.

After 12:00 preceding duty with the same transfer, explicitly record the approved calculation order before selecting 12:00 versus 12:30; the implementation must not silently choose between the interpretations.
A rest interval meeting the duration threshold still fails if it does not contain an eight-hour sleep opportunity in addition to travel and physiological needs.
At exactly 30 minutes travelling time the AMC travel-excess adjustment is zero; above 30 minutes it is twice the excess, retaining the one-hour physiological allowance.
scenario_note: These scenarios illustrate source meaning and interpretation choices for documentary review. They are not acceptance requirements for a local evaluator or executable compliance tests.

title: Recurrent extended recovery rest
source_text:
### ORO.FTL.235(d), (e) — regulatory requirements

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(d)   Recurrent extended recovery rest periods
      Flight time specification schemes shall specify recurrent extended recovery rest periods to
      compensate for cumulative fatigue. The minimum recurrent extended recovery rest period shall
      be 36 hours, including 2 local nights, and in any case the time between the end of one recurrent
      extended recovery rest period and the start of the next extended recovery rest period shall not
      be more than 168 hours. The recurrent extended recovery rest period shall be increased to 2
      local days twice every month.
(e)   Flight time specification schemes shall specify additional rest periods in accordance with the
      applicable certification specifications to compensate for:
      (1)   the effects of time zone differences and extensions of the FDP;
      (2)   additional cumulative fatigue due to disruptive schedules; and
      (3)   a change of home base.
```

### ORO.FTL.105 definitions (15, 16, 21, 8, 9)

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(15) ‘local day’ means a 24-hour period commencing at 00:00 local time;

(16) ‘local night’ means a period of 8 hours falling between 22:00 and 08:00 local time;

(21) ‘rest period’ means a continuous, uninterrupted and defined period of time, following duty or
     prior to duty, during which a crew member is free of all duties, standby and reserve.

(8)   ‘disruptive schedule’ means a crew member’s roster which disrupts the sleep opportunity
      during the optimal sleep time window by comprising an FDP or a combination of FDPs which
      encroach, start or finish during any portion of the day or of the night where a crew member is
      acclimatised. A schedule may be disruptive due to early starts, late finishes or night duties.
      (a)   ‘early type’ of disruptive schedule means:
            (i)    for ‘early start’ a duty period starting in the period between 05:00 and 05:59 in the
                   time zone to which a crew member is acclimatised, and
            (ii)   for ‘late finish’ a duty period finishing in the period between 23:00 and 01:59 in the
                   time zone to which a crew member is acclimatised;
      (b)   ‘late type’ of disruptive schedule means:
            (i)    for ‘early start’ a duty period starting in the period between 05:00 and 06:59 in the
                   time zone to which a crew member is acclimatised; and
            (ii)   for ‘late finish’ a duty period finishing in the period between 00:00 and 01:59 in the
                   time zone to which a crew member is acclimatised;

(9)   ‘night duty’ means a duty period encroaching any portion of the period between 02:00 and
      04:59 in the time zone to which the crew is acclimatised;
```

### CS FTL.1.235(a) — disruptive-schedule compensation

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(a)   Disruptive schedules
      (1)   If a transition from a late finish/night duty to an early start is planned at home base, the
            rest period between the 2 FDPs includes 1 local night.
      (2)   If a crew member performs 4 or more night duties, early starts or late finishes between
            2 extended recovery rest periods as defined in ORO.FTL.235(d), the second extended
            recovery rest period is extended to 60 hours.
```

### GM1 ORO.FTL.230(a) — explanatory guidance

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
GM1 ORO.FTL.230(a) Reserve

ROSTERING OF RESERVE
Including reserve in a roster, also referred to as ‘rostering’, implies that a reserve period that does not
result in a duty period may not retrospectively be considered as part of a recurrent extended recovery
rest period.
```
notes: Edition/scope note (explanatory, not a quotation): EASA Easy Access Rules for Air Operations, Revision 24, March 2026, preserved official edition; PDF viewer and printed page numbers agree. ORO.FTL.100 (p. 854) addresses CAT aeroplanes. CS FTL.1.100 (p. 874) covers scheduled and charter aeroplane CAT, excluding EMS, air taxi and single-pilot operations. ORO.FTL.125 (p. 865) requires an operation-appropriate, competent-authority-approved flight time specification scheme; preserve applicable approved-scheme choices and operator procedures. ORO requirements, CS certification specifications, AMC acceptable means of compliance and GM guidance have different status. This source record makes no claim about amendments after Revision 24.

Measure the 168-hour gap from the end of one qualifying recovery rest to the start of the next. Local nights and local days require local-calendar containment, not merely elapsed duration. Preserve the applicable early/late disruptive-schedule classification and count relevant duties between qualifying recovery rests. The twice-per-month requirement needs an explicit event attribution convention.
illustrative_scenarios: 168:00 from the end of one qualifying recovery rest to the start of the next meets the gap ceiling; 168:01 fails.
Rest from 08:00 Monday to 20:00 Tuesday lasts 36 hours but contains only one qualifying local night, so it fails the two-local-night condition.
The twice-per-month increase contains two complete local days under the local-midnight definition; arbitrary 48-hour elapsed breaks do not automatically satisfy it.
Four relevant night duties, early starts or late finishes between recovery rests require the second recovery rest to reach 60:00; three do not trigger this particular extension.
A planned late-finish/night-duty to early-start transition at home base has a rest containing one local night. Reserve without an assignment is not retrospectively relabelled as recovery rest.
scenario_note: These scenarios illustrate source meaning and interpretation choices for documentary review. They are not acceptance requirements for a local evaluator or executable compliance tests.

title: Split duty
source_text:
### ORO.FTL.220 — regulatory requirement

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
ORO.FTL.220 Split duty

The conditions for extending the basic maximum daily FDP due to a break on the ground shall be in
accordance with the following:
(a)   flight time specification schemes shall specify the following elements for split duty in
      accordance with the certification specifications applicable to the type of operation:
      (1)   the minimum duration of a break on the ground; and
      (2)   the possibility to extend the FDP prescribed under point ORO.FTL.205(b) taking into
            account the duration of the break on the ground, the facilities provided to the crew
            member to rest and other relevant factors;
(b)   the break on the ground shall count in full as FDP;
(c)   split duty shall not follow a reduced rest.
```

### CS FTL.1.220 — complete governing certification specification

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
CS FTL.1.220 Split duty

The increase of limits on flight duty, under the provisions of ORO.FTL.220, complies with the following:
(a)   The break on the ground within the FDP has a minimum duration of 3 consecutive hours.
(b)   The break excludes the time allowed for post and pre-flight duties and travelling. The minimum
      total time for post and pre-flight duties and travelling is 30 minutes. The operator specifies the
      actual times in its operations manual.
(c)   The maximum FDP specified in ORO.FTL.205(b) may be increased by up to 50 % of the break.
(d)   Suitable accommodation is provided either for a break of 6 hours or more or for a break that
      encroaches the window of circadian low (WOCL).
(e)   In all other cases:
      (1)    accommodation is provided; and
      (2)    any time of the actual break exceeding 6 hours or any time of the break that encroaches
             the WOCL does not count for the extension of the FDP.
(f)   Split duty cannot be combined with in-flight rest.
```

### ORO.FTL.105 definitions (6, 3, 4, 28)

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(6)   ‘break’ means a period of time within an flight duty period, shorter than a rest period, counting
      as duty and during which a crew member is free of all tasks;

(3)    ‘accommodation’ means, for the purpose of standby and split duty, a quiet and comfortable
       place not open to the public with the ability to control light and temperature, equipped with
       adequate furniture that provides a crew member with the possibility to sleep, with enough
       capacity to accommodate all crew members present at the same time and with access to food
       and drink;

(4)   ‘suitable accommodation’ means, for the purpose of standby, split duty and rest, a separate
      room for each crew member located in a quiet environment and equipped with a bed, which is
      sufficiently ventilated, has a device for regulating temperature and light intensity, and access to
      food and drink;

(28) ‘window of circadian low ('WOCL') means the period between 02:00 and 05:59 hours in the time
     zone to which a crew member is acclimatised.
```

### ORO.FTL.205(d)(4) — combination prohibition

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(4)     Extension of the maximum basic daily FDP without in-flight rest shall not be combined
              with extensions due to in-flight rest or split duty in the same duty period.
```

### GM1 CS FTL.1.220(b) — explanatory guidance

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
GM1 CS FTL.1.220(b) Split duty

POST, PRE-FLIGHT DUTY AND TRAVELLING TIMES
The operator should specify post and pre-flight duty and travelling times taking into account aircraft
type, type of operation and airport conditions.
```
source_references: CS FTL.1.220; GM1 CS FTL.1.220(b), p. 882
notes: Edition/scope note (explanatory, not a quotation): EASA Easy Access Rules for Air Operations, Revision 24, March 2026, preserved official edition; PDF viewer and printed page numbers agree. ORO.FTL.100 (p. 854) addresses CAT aeroplanes. CS FTL.1.100 (p. 874) covers scheduled and charter aeroplane CAT, excluding EMS, air taxi and single-pilot operations. ORO.FTL.125 (p. 865) requires an operation-appropriate, competent-authority-approved flight time specification scheme; preserve applicable approved-scheme choices and operator procedures. ORO requirements, CS certification specifications, AMC acceptable means of compliance and GM guidance have different status. This source record makes no claim about amendments after Revision 24.

Use the net consecutive task-free break after operator-specified duty/travel exclusions, with the combined exclusion at least 30 minutes. The full break stays inside measured FDP. Retain both CS clauses (d) and (e): clipping extension credit cannot excuse missing suitable accommodation when (d) requires it. Reduced-rest, split-duty, in-flight-rest and planned-extension combination conditions must be linked.
illustrative_scenarios: Ground time 3:30 minus 0:30 of post/pre-flight duties and travel leaves a qualifying three-consecutive-hour break and permits at most 1:30 FDP extension; ground time 3:00 with the same exclusion does not qualify.
The whole break remains inside measured FDP, including when its credited duration increases the FDP limit.
A break of exactly six hours requires suitable accommodation; any break encroaching the WOCL also requires suitable accommodation.
With accommodation under CS (e), excluded WOCL time or time beyond six hours earns no extension credit, and clipping credit never excuses a facility requirement under CS (d).
An otherwise qualifying break after reduced rest fails split-duty eligibility; split duty cannot combine with in-flight rest or the planned extension without in-flight rest.
scenario_note: These scenarios illustrate source meaning and interpretation choices for documentary review. They are not acceptance requirements for a local evaluator or executable compliance tests.

title: Standby accounting and FDP impact
source_text:
### ORO.FTL.225 — complete regulatory requirement

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
ORO.FTL.225 Standby and duties at the airport

If an operator assigns crew members to standby or to any duty at the airport, the following shall apply
in accordance with the certification specifications applicable to the type of operation:
(a)   standby and any duty at the airport shall be in the roster and the start and end time of standby
      shall be defined and notified in advance to the crew members concerned to provide them with
      the opportunity to plan adequate rest;
(b)   a crew member is considered on airport standby from reporting at the reporting point until the
      end of the notified airport standby period;
(c)   airport standby shall count in full as duty period for the purpose of points ORO.FTL.210 and
      ORO.FTL.235;
(d)   any duty at the airport shall count in full as duty period and the FDP shall count in full from the
      airport duty reporting time;
(e)   the operator shall provide accommodation to the crew member on airport standby;
(f)   flight time specification schemes shall specify the following elements:

      (1)    the maximum duration of any standby;
      (2)    the impact of the time spent on standby on the maximum FDP that may be assigned,
             taking into account facilities provided to the crew member to rest, and other relevant
             factors such as:
             —      the need for immediate readiness of the crew member,
             —      the interference of standby with sleep, and
             —      sufficient notification to protect a sleep opportunity between the call for duty and
                    the assigned FDP;
      (3)    the minimum rest period following standby which does not lead to assignment of an FDP;
      (4)    how time spent on standby other than airport standby shall be counted for the purpose
             of cumulative duty periods.
```

### CS FTL.1.225 — complete governing certification specification

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
CS FTL.1.225 Standby

The modification of limits on flight duty, duty and rest periods under the provisions of ORO.FTL.225
complies with the following:

(a)   Airport standby
      (1)   If not leading to the assignment of an FDP, airport standby is followed by a rest period as
            specified in ORO.FTL.235.
      (2)   If an assigned FDP starts during airport standby, the following applies:
            (i)    the FDP counts from the start of the FDP. The maximum FDP is reduced by any time
                   spent on standby in excess of 4 hours;
            (ii)   the maximum combined duration of airport standby and assigned FDP as specified
                   in ORO.FTL.205(b) and (d) is 16 hours.
(b)   Standby other than airport standby:
      (1)   the maximum duration of standby other than airport standby is 16 hours;
      (2)   The operator’s standby procedures are designed to ensure that the combination of
            standby and FDP do not lead to more than 18 hours awake time;
      (3)   25 % of time spent on standby other than airport standby counts as duty time for the
            purpose of ORO.FTL.210;
      (4)   standby is followed by a rest period in accordance with ORO.FTL.235;
      (5)   standby ceases when the crew member reports at the designated reporting point;
      (6)   if standby ceases within the first 6 hours, the maximum FDP counts from reporting;
      (7)   if standby ceases after the first 6 hours, the maximum FDP is reduced by the amount of
            standby time exceeding 6 hours;
      (8)   if the FDP is extended due to in-flight rest according to CS FTL.1.205(c), or to split duty
            according to CS FTL.1.220, the 6 hours of paragraph (6) and (7) are extended to 8 hours;
      (9)   if standby starts between 23:00 and 07:00, the time between 23:00 and 07:00 does not
            count towards the reduction of the FDP under (6), (7) and (8) until the crew member is
            contacted by the operator; and
      (10) the response time between call and reporting time established by the operator allows
           the crew member to arrive from his/her place of rest to the designated reporting point
           within a reasonable time.
```

### ORO.FTL.105 definitions (25, 26, 27, 3, 4)

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(25) ‘standby’ means a pre-notified and defined period of time during which a crew member is
     required by the operator to be available to receive an assignment for a flight, positioning or
     other duty without an intervening rest period.

(26) ‘airport standby’ means a standby performed at the airport;

(27) ‘other standby’ means a standby either at home or in a suitable accommodation;

(3)    ‘accommodation’ means, for the purpose of standby and split duty, a quiet and comfortable
       place not open to the public with the ability to control light and temperature, equipped with
       adequate furniture that provides a crew member with the possibility to sleep, with enough
       capacity to accommodate all crew members present at the same time and with access to food
       and drink;

(4)   ‘suitable accommodation’ means, for the purpose of standby, split duty and rest, a separate
      room for each crew member located in a quiet environment and equipped with a bed, which is
      sufficiently ventilated, has a device for regulating temperature and light intensity, and access to
      food and drink;
```

### GM1 CS FTL.1.225, GM1 CS FTL.1.225(b), GM1 CS FTL.1.225(b)(2) — explanatory guidance

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
GM1 CS FTL.1.225 Standby

MINIMUM REST AND STANDBY
(a)   If airport or other standby initially assigned is reduced by the operator during standby that does
      not lead to an assignment to a flight duty period, the minimum rest requirements specified in
      ORO.FTL.235 should apply.
(b)   If a minimum rest period as specified in ORO.FTL.235 is provided before reporting for the duty
      assigned during the standby, this time period should not count as standby duty.
(c)   Standby other than airport standby counts (partly) as duty for the purpose of ORO.FTL.210 only.
      If a crew member receives an assignment during standby other than airport standby, the actual
      reporting time at the designated reporting point should be used for the purpose of
      ORO.FTL.235.

GM1 CS FTL.1.225(b) Standby

STANDBY OTHER THAN AIRPORT STANDBY NOTIFICATION
Operator procedures for the notification of assigned duties during standby other than airport standby
should avoid interference with sleeping patterns if possible.

GM1 CS FTL.1.225(b)(2) Standby

AWAKE TIME
Scientific research shows that continuous awake in excess of 18 hours can reduce the alertness and
should be avoided.
```
notes: Edition/scope note (explanatory, not a quotation): EASA Easy Access Rules for Air Operations, Revision 24, March 2026, preserved official edition; PDF viewer and printed page numbers agree. ORO.FTL.100 (p. 854) addresses CAT aeroplanes. CS FTL.1.100 (p. 874) covers scheduled and charter aeroplane CAT, excluding EMS, air taxi and single-pilot operations. ORO.FTL.125 (p. 865) requires an operation-appropriate, competent-authority-approved flight time specification scheme; preserve applicable approved-scheme choices and operator procedures. ORO requirements, CS certification specifications, AMC acceptable means of compliance and GM guidance have different status. This source record makes no claim about amendments after Revision 24.

Use distinct ledgers for cumulative duty, rest, FDP reduction and awake time. Airport standby plus assigned-FDP 16-hour cap expressly cites ORO.FTL.205(b)/(d); preserve that scope. The 18-hour awake provision governs procedure design and is not proved solely by a roster arithmetic check. Overnight exclusion requires standby-start and operator-contact events. Operator response time, notification, accommodation and subsequent rest remain obligations.
illustrative_scenarios: Five hours of airport standby reduces the ordinary maximum FDP by one hour and contributes all five hours to duty; for the cited ORO.FTL.205(b)/(d) scope, combined standby plus assigned FDP cannot exceed 16:00.

Eight hours of other standby contributes 2:00 to cumulative duty and reduces an ordinary FDP cap by 2:00; with a qualifying in-flight-rest or split-duty extension, the eight-hour threshold produces no reduction.
Other standby beginning at 23:00 with first operator contact at 05:00 excludes protected pre-contact overnight time from the FDP reduction; preserve contact and report events.
Other standby 16:00 meets its duration ceiling and 16:01 fails; separately assess procedures intended to prevent standby plus FDP producing more than 18 hours awake.
Standby without an assigned FDP is followed by the applicable rest; verify roster notification, defined start/end and airport accommodation independently of numerical FDP compliance.
scenario_note: These scenarios illustrate source meaning and interpretation choices for documentary review. They are not acceptance requirements for a local evaluator or executable compliance tests.

title: Augmentation and in-flight rest
source_text:
### ORO.FTL.205(e) — regulatory requirement

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(e)   Maximum daily FDP with the use of extensions due to in-flight rest
      Flight time specification schemes shall specify the conditions for extensions of the maximum
      basic daily FDP with in-flight rest in accordance with the certification specifications applicable
      to the type of operation, taking into account:
      (i)     the number of sectors flown;
      (ii)    the minimum in-flight rest allocated to each crew member;
      (iii)   the type of in-flight rest facilities; and
      (iv)    the augmentation of the basic flight crew.
```

### ORO.FTL.105 definitions (5, 19, 17)

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(5)   ‘augmented flight crew’ means a flight crew which comprises more than the minimum number
      required to operate the aircraft, allowing each flight crew member to leave the assigned post,
      for the purpose of in-flight rest, and to be replaced by another appropriately qualified flight
      crew member;

(19) ‘rest facility’ means a bunk or seat with leg and foot support suitable for crew members'
     sleeping on board an aircraft.

(17) ‘operating crew member’ means a crew member carrying out duties in an aircraft during a
     sector;
```

### CS FTL.1.205(c), definitions and (1)–(7) — complete governing certification specification, with exact cabin-rest table transcription

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(c)   Extension of FDP due to in-flight rest
      In-flight rest facilities in accordance with ORO.FTL.205(e)(iii) fulfil the following minimum
      standards:
      —     ‘Class 1 rest facility’ means a bunk or other surface that allows for a flat or near flat
            sleeping position. It reclines to at least 80° back angle to the vertical and is located
            separately from both the flight crew compartment and the passenger cabin in an area
            that allows the crew member to control light, and provides isolation from noise and
            disturbance;
      —     ‘Class 2 rest facility’ means a seat in an aircraft cabin that reclines at least 45° back angle
            to the vertical, has at least a pitch of 55 inches (137,5 cm), a seat width of at least 20
            inches (50 cm) and provides leg and foot support. It is separated from passengers by at
            least a curtain to provide darkness and some sound mitigation, and is reasonably free
            from disturbance by passengers or crew members;
      —     ‘Class 3 rest facility’ means a seat in an aircraft cabin or flight crew compartment that
            reclines at least 40° from the vertical, provides leg and foot support and is separated from
            passengers by at least a curtain to provide darkness and some sound mitigation, and is
            not adjacent to any seat occupied by passengers.
      (1)   The extension of FDP with in-flight rest under the provisions of ORO.FTL.205(e) complies
            with the following:
            (i)    the FDP is limited to 3 sectors; and
            (ii)   the minimum in-flight rest period is a consecutive 90-minute period for each crew
                   member and 2 consecutive hours for the flight crew members at control during
                   landing.
      (2)   The maximum daily FDP under the provisions of ORO.FTL.205(e) may be extended due to
            in-flight rest for flight crew:
            (i)    with one additional flight crew member:
                   (A)   up to 14 hours with class 3 rest facilities;
                   (B)   up to 15 hours with class 2 rest facilities; or
                   (C)   up to 16 hours with class 1 rest facilities;
            (ii)   with two additional flight crew members:
                   (A)   up to 15 hours with class 3 rest facilities;
                   (B)   up to 16 hours with class 2 rest facilities; or
                   (C)   up to 17 hours with class 1 rest facilities.

      (3)   The minimum in-flight rest for each cabin crew member is:
                                                           Minimum in-flight rest (in hours)
              Maximum extended FDP
                                                 Class 1               Class 2                 Class 3
             up to 14:30 hrs              1:30                  1:30                    1:30
             14:31 – 15:00 hrs            1:45                  2:00                    2:20
             15:01 – 15:30 hrs            2:00                  2:20                    2:40
             15:31 – 16:00 hrs            2:15                  2:40                    3:00
             16:01 – 16:30 hrs            2:35                  3:00                    Not allowed
             16:31 – 17:00 hrs            3:00                  3:25                    Not allowed
             17:01 – 17:30 hrs            3:25                  Not allowed             Not allowed
             17:31 – 18:00 hrs            3:50                  Not allowed             Not allowed

      (4)   The limits specified in (2) may be increased by 1 hour for FDPs that include 1 sector of
            more than 9 hours of continuous flight time and a maximum of 2 sectors.
      (5)   All time spent in the rest facility is counted as FDP.
      (6)   The minimum rest at destination is at least as long as the preceding duty period, or 14
            hours, whichever is greater.
      (7)   A crew member does not start a positioning sector to become part of this operating crew
            on the same flight.
```

### ORO.FTL.205(d)(4) — combination prohibition

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(4)     Extension of the maximum basic daily FDP without in-flight rest shall not be combined
              with extensions due to in-flight rest or split duty in the same duty period.
```

### CS FTL.1.220(f) — combination prohibition

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
(f)   Split duty cannot be combined with in-flight rest.
```

### GM1 ORO.FTL.105(17) — explanatory guidance

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
GM1 ORO.FTL.105(17) Definitions

OPERATING CREW MEMBER
A person on board an aircraft is either a crew member or a passenger. If a crew member is not a
passenger on board an aircraft he/she should be considered as ‘carrying out duties’. The crew member
remains an operating crew member during in-flight rest. In-flight rest counts in full as FDP, and for the
purpose of ORO.FTL.210.
```

### GM1–2 CS FTL.1.205(c)(1)(ii) — explanatory guidance

Verbatim quotation (line wrapping and layout whitespace normalized):

```text
GM1 CS FTL.1.205(c)(1)(ii) Flight Duty Period (FDP)

IN-FLIGHT REST
In-flight rest should be taken during the cruise phase of the flight.

GM2 CS FTL.1.205(c)(1)(ii) Flight Duty Period (FDP)

IN-FLIGHT REST
In-flight rest periods should be allocated in order to optimise the alertness of those flight crew
members at control during landing.
```
notes: Edition/scope note (explanatory, not a quotation): EASA Easy Access Rules for Air Operations, Revision 24, March 2026, preserved official edition; PDF viewer and printed page numbers agree. ORO.FTL.100 (p. 854) addresses CAT aeroplanes. CS FTL.1.100 (p. 874) covers scheduled and charter aeroplane CAT, excluding EMS, air taxi and single-pilot operations. ORO.FTL.125 (p. 865) requires an operation-appropriate, competent-authority-approved flight time specification scheme; preserve applicable approved-scheme choices and operator procedures. ORO requirements, CS certification specifications, AMC acceptable means of compliance and GM guidance have different status. This source record makes no claim about amendments after Revision 24.

The 14/15/16 and 15/16/17-hour values are total maximum FDPs for one and two additional qualified flight crew, not increments to the basic table. Do not extrapolate an entitlement for three or more additional crew. The additional hour requires a maximum of two sectors and one sector with strictly more than nine hours of continuous flight time; do not silently substitute aggregate block time.

Each crew member requires 90 consecutive minutes and flight crew at control during landing require two consecutive hours. CS (3) sets the larger cabin minimum without separately saying that all of that larger amount must be consecutive; retain this distinction and any approved-scheme conditions. Identifying usable facilities and non-overlapping capacity is an inferred allocation requirement, not a separately quoted EASA numerical cap. GM cruise/alertness recommendations remain guidance.

The cabin table uses minute-labelled bands; explicitly define treatment of subminute input such as 14:30:30. “Not allowed” must be a prohibition, not a missing value or fallback. The cabin table does not independently authorize an 18-hour flight-crew FDP. All rest-facility time remains FDP; destination rest is max(preceding full duty, 14 hours); preserve the same-flight positioning prohibition and extension-combination prohibitions.
illustrative_scenarios: One additional qualified flight crew member permits maximum FDP 14:00/15:00/16:00 for class 3/2/1; two permit 15:00/16:00/17:00. Treat them as total limits and reject unsupported extrapolation to three or more additional crew.

With at most two sectors, exactly 9:00 continuous flight in the longest sector earns no extra hour; strictly more than 9:00 can earn it. Three sectors never receive that bonus, even with a sector over nine hours.

Each crew member, including cabin crew, has at least 90 consecutive minutes of in-flight rest; flight crew at control during landing have two consecutive hours. Two separate one-hour intervals do not meet the landing-crew condition.

At extended FDP 16:00 class 3 cabin rest has a 3:00 minimum; at 16:01 class 3 is Not allowed, while class 1 requires 2:35 and class 2 requires 3:00. Keep the separate 90-minute continuity floor without asserting that the entire larger cabin-table total must be consecutive.
Actual facility allocations satisfy their class criteria and simultaneous capacity, all time in them remains FDP, and destination rest is at least max(preceding full duty, 14:00).

A crew member cannot start positioning and become operating crew on that same flight; an in-flight-rest extension cannot combine with split duty or the planned no-in-flight-rest extension. A failed eligibility condition remains a violation rather than disappearing as not applicable.
scenario_note: These scenarios illustrate source meaning and interpretation choices for documentary review. They are not acceptance requirements for a local evaluator or executable compliance tests.
